items.name: Millau Viaduct
items.caption: Crews launched the steel deck from both sides of the Tarn valley.
items.detail: Temporary steel piers shortened the spans during launching. The two halves met above the Tarn in May 2004.
items.image_alt: Illustration of Millau Viaduct’s steel deck advancing across the Tarn valley on temporary supports

items.name: Sydney Opera House
items.caption: The roof shells share the geometry of a single sphere.
items.detail: The common geometry let crews cast standardized concrete rib segments on site and lift them into place. The Opera House opened in 1973.
items.image_alt: Artistic reconstruction of the Sydney Opera House roof under construction, with exposed concrete ribs above the harbour.

items.name: Hoover Dam
items.caption: Water circulating through pipes cooled the dam’s concrete as it cured.
items.detail: Crews poured the concrete in blocks and ran river water, then chilled water, through embedded steel coils. The dam was dedicated in 1935.
items.image_alt: Artistic reconstruction of the stepped concrete pours and overhead cableway at Hoover Dam under construction in Black Canyon.

items.name: Gotthard Base Tunnel
items.caption: Gripper shoes braced against the tunnel walls so the cutterhead could push into rock.
items.detail: Sissi broke through the east tube in 2010. The tunnel officially opened on 1 June 2016, and scheduled trains began running on 11 December.
items.image_alt: Artistic cutaway reconstruction of the Sissi tunnel borer, with a circular cutterhead against the rock face, thrust cylinders and a gripper shoe braced against the sidewall.

items.name: Gateway Arch
items.caption: Climbing derricks lifted steel sections while a temporary truss braced the arch legs.
items.detail: The last section joined the legs on 28 October 1965. The north tram first carried the public on 24 July 1967.
items.image_alt: Artistic reconstruction of the unfinished Gateway Arch, with a steel truss between its legs and a climbing derrick mounted on each leg.

items.name: Guggenheim Museum Bilbao
items.caption: CATIA turned Gehry’s complex curves into geometry that builders could use.
items.detail: Construction ran from 1993 to 1997. The museum was inaugurated on 18 October 1997 and opened to the public the next day.
items.image_alt: Artistic reconstruction of Guggenheim Museum Bilbao under construction, with titanium cladding beside exposed curved steel framing on the riverfront.

items.name: Abu Simbel Temples Relocation
items.caption: Crews cut the temples into blocks and rebuilt them above the rising reservoir.
items.detail: Stone blocks were catalogued and reassembled inside a new artificial hill. The relocated temples were inaugurated on 22 September 1968.
items.image_alt: Artistic reconstruction of a crane lifting a sawn Ramses II head block beside scaffolded statue sections during the Abu Simbel relocation.

items.name: Golden Gate Bridge
items.location: San Francisco–Marin County, California, United States
items.caption: Workers spun the main cables in place, carrying individual wires over the towers.
items.detail: Parallel wire strands were compacted into each main cable. Pedestrians crossed on 27 May 1937, followed by vehicle traffic on 28 May.
items.image_alt: Artistic reconstruction of Golden Gate Bridge cable spinning, with workers on a temporary catwalk beside a wheeled carrier and parallel wire strands.

items.name: Eiffel Tower
items.caption: Temporary hydraulic cylinders helped align the first-floor ironwork.
items.detail: Hand pumps adjusted two columns before permanent wedges replaced the cylinders. Completed and inaugurated 31 March 1889; public opening 15 May.
items.image_alt: Artistic reconstruction of Eiffel Tower first-floor assembly, with an enlarged temporary hydraulic cylinder and hand pump at a column base and timber falsework behind.

items.name: Brunelleschi’s Dome
items.caption: Herringbone brickwork helped stabilize the dome as its inclined courses rose.
items.detail: Brunelleschi built without full wooden centering. Successive masonry rings closed as work rose. The dome body was completed on 30 August 1436; the lantern came later.
items.image_alt: Artistic cutaway reconstruction of Brunelleschi’s dome under construction, with masons laying upright herringbone bricks among sloping courses beside an exposed double-shell edge.

items.name: Falkirk Wheel
items.caption: Bolted site joints joined the segmented arms of the rotating boat lift.
items.detail: Crews preassembled major sections at low level before crane lifts. Main erection finished in September 2001; the Wheel officially opened on 24 May 2002.
items.image_alt: Artistic reconstruction of Falkirk Wheel arm preassembly, with workers tightening a bolted splice beside a large gondola-ring opening on ground supports.
